text:
incident-bot: ALERT: memcloud.api (managed cache) is returning 502/504 for token-lookup endpoints used by rl-cluster-eu. Error rate jumped from 0.5/s -> 45/s in last 4m. Auto-paging oncall. Logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/memcloud/stream/def456 :rotating_light:

nina (oncall): I'm oncall. paging @sam and @infra-lee. quick check: is this auth failures or gateway?

sam: looking at traces — upstream returns are 502 Bad Gateway with body `503 downstream overloaded` in many traces. No 4xx auth codes. Connection resets also seen.

kevin (support): customer-facing queue: handful of support tickets about higher-than-usual 429s and one partner reported delayed embeddings. No major outages yet. I'll prepare a short status blurb.

infra-lee: grafana: auth-lookup error-rate and request latency spike. rate-limiter falls back to cached decisions in localstore leading to higher allow-rate so downstream throttles don't kick in — customers see bursts then 429s.

nina (oncall): immediate mitigations to consider: 1) switch rate limiter to slow-path reject-on-cache-miss (more conservative but increases denied requests) 2) route cache lookups to fallback cache proxy we maintain (cache-fallback.redwood-internal) 3) increase local TTL so fewer lookups but may stale decisions. Thoughts?

sam: option 2 is fast if fallback is healthy. fallback has cold keys but will likely reduce 502 surface. Option 1 is risky for customer experience. prefer 2+3: route memcloud -> cache-fallback and bump local TTL by 300s.

ops-bot: Posting incident banner: "Investigating elevated cache errors impacting rate limiting; mitigation in progress."

nina (oncall): infra-lee, can you toggle the routing rule for rl-cluster-eu to prefer cache-fallback? If warmup needed, we'll do canary.

infra-lee: preparing a service routing change. plan: update ConfigMap `rl-cache-routing` for namespace prod-eu: set primary=cache-fallback, secondary=memcloud, with weighted traffic 10% fallback -> 90% memcloud for canary, then 100% fallback if stable.

sam: I'll also push env var RATE_LIMITER_LOCAL_TTL=300 for rl-cluster-eu. small CPU impact expected.

nina (oncall): proceed with canary. watch auth-lookup 5xx, rate-limiter error rates, customer 429s.

infra-lee: executing kubectl patch: ```kubectl -n prod-eu set env deployment/rl-cluster --env="RATE_LIMITER_LOCAL_TTL=300" && kubectl -n prod-eu apply -f configs/rl-cache-routing-canary.yaml```

incident-bot: ROUTING CHANGE STARTED by infra-lee (canary=1/1).

sam: canary looks good at 90s. memcloud 502s for canary pod dropped to ~5% of previous and overall rl auth errors down 60%.

kevin (support): updating status: "Partial mitigation in place, routing to fallback cache. Some customers continue to see transient rate limiting — we're monitoring and will update."

infra-lee: promoting to 50% -> 100% over next 4m. all pods now using cache-fallback as primary.

nina (oncall): confirm metrics: auth-lookup 5xx near baseline, rl CPU +10% but within thresholds, customer 429s decreasing. Good. Marking mitigation as successful for now.

sam: opened vendor ticket with MemCloud: https://memcloud.status/tickets/RW-1234. included traces, sample 502 bodies, timestamps. Vendor-bot responded: "we're investigating a backend proxy issue in eu-west that affected certain POPs; rolling fix".

vendor-memcloud-bot: [MemCloud] Acknowledged RW-1234. Root cause: degraded proxy pool causing 502s; mitigation in progress. ETA 20-40m.

kevin (support): customers impacted: 6 enterprise customers saw increased 429s for ~18 minutes before mitigation; 24 dev accounts briefly saw elevated latency. drafting CS email to the 6 with timeline and mitigation steps.

nina (oncall): handoff checklist for the next shift: 1) keep monitoring rl.auth_5xx and rl.local_cache_hits 2) verify memcloud vendor status and update ticket 3) prepare to revert routing once vendor healthy (we prefer restoring memcloud as primary to avoid stale decisions) 4) postmortem owners: sam/infra-lee.

infra-lee: adding runbook entry: `if cache provider 5xx spike => route to cache-fallback; raise cpu budget if TTL increased; notify support`. Also added test script: ```bash
# verify fallback behavior
curl -sS https://cache-fallback.internal/health | jq .status
python3 tools/simulate_rl_calls.py --env prod-eu --count 50
```

sam: also note improvement threshold: only revert when memcloud 5xx < 1/s and latency < 50ms for 10m. I'll attach that to vendor ticket and our automation.

kevin (support): posted customer email draft and the status page updated.

nina (oncall): marking incident mitigated from customer-impact POV. we'll keep this open for vendor fix confirmation and postmortem. thanks team. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident banner updated: "Mitigation applied: traffic routed to internal cache-fallback. Vendor investigating MemCloud proxy issue."

sam: closing action items: collect traces and a short timeline, confirm vendor fix before revert, write postmortem with recommendations: 1) add automated failover for cache 5xx above threshold 2) add canary checks for provider health 3) consider multi-provider routing for global POPs.

nina (oncall): handing off to night SRE: infra-lee. if memcloud posts update we'll run verification and then revert routing on approval. leaving handoff notes in #oncall-handoffs.

infra-lee: ack. monitoring dashboards added for night shift.

kevin (support): will follow up with customers after final vendor confirmation.

incident-bot: paging cleared."
